storm-producer-wiring.summary: The fence covers the seam owners (box.py for the ContextVar binding, daemon.py for the session wrapper, and storm.py) plus the one predecessor dormancy test that the new daemon-to-storm import breaks. The criteria can all be met together without contradicting merged behavior, and the ticket builds exactly the storm-producer-wiring machinery that section 20 grants.

storm-notification-activation.summary: The ticket is buildable. The fence covers the storm/box/daemon seams, the production root `squatch/__main__.py` where `_RestartRunner.session` is wrapped, and both test files whose dormancy assertions must change. All five Box construction sites already call `Box.enqueue` inside `runner.session()`, including triage through `_triage_pass`, so the predecessor's call-time binding reaches them without edits.

phase3-continue-17.summary: The ticket authors storm-dispatch-hold as dormant construction only and defers production activation to 'a later production owner'. Section 20's finite registry names no such owner, and its only storm suppression entry is storm-dispatch-hold itself, so the plan has to decide who activates the hold before this batch can be authored.

findings.message: Section 20 says 'Dispatch suppression remains OUT until the separate KNOWN-DEEP storm-dispatch-hold admission', which means storm-dispatch-hold is the admission that turns suppression on. The registry grants it only storm/control/daemon plus tests/test_storm_hold.py. That fence has no production root (squatch/__main__.py) and no composition harness (tests/test_daemon_composition.py). The plan also has no clarification like the one for kill-cli-activation and DaemonTasks, which names the later owner of a dormant boundary. The ticket fills the gap itself: it tells storm-dispatch-hold to stay dormant, forbids activating it in the bootstrap drain/run composition, and says 'No new activation seed is authored here'. The carried suffix [[storm-dispatch-hold], [checkpoint-push], [daemon-soak], [soak-run], [phase3-exit]] has no seed that activates the hold. Trips would then be produced in production, but dispatch would never be suppressed before phase3-exit, and the deferral would point to a phase-3 owner that does not exist. Re-authoring cannot fix this within the caps. Activating inside storm-dispatch-hold would need fence entries the registry does not grant. Adding an activation seed would add an admission the finite registry does not list. Keeping it dormant contradicts the plan.
findings.paved_road: Fix section 20 first. Either (a) declare storm-dispatch-hold a construction+activation singleton and grant it squatch/__main__.py and tests/test_daemon_composition.py (and squatch/drain.py if needed) with a render/Context partition, or (b) add a storm-hold-activation admission to the finite registry and the ordered suffix, with its own fence and the negative assertions it migrates. Then rerun phase3-continue-17 so it carries the repaired suffix and ownership.
